about: The land layer: see tools/build_land_layer.py and MECHANICS.md, 'Resources and the land'.
encoding: one byte per node; value = min + byte / 255 * (max - min); sea = 0

chelsa.name: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122)

etopo.name: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

kk10.name: KK10 anthropogenic land cover change (Kaplan et al. 2011, The Holocene 21:775-791)

sites.name: Facsimilia historical sites (tools/land_sites.json), from standard reference works

fields.name: elevation
fields.description: Average height above sea level
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: slope
fields.description: Average steepness
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: flat_share
fields.description: Share of the land gentle enough to plough (under 3 degrees)
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: ruggedness
fields.description: How much the height varies within the place
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: southness
fields.description: Whether slopes face south (sunny, good for vines) or north
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: coast_km
fields.description: Distance to the sea
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: shallows
fields.description: Share of the nearby sea shallower than 50 m: fish nurseries, shellfish, easy landings
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: temp_mean
fields.description: Average yearly temperature
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: temp_summer
fields.description: Average daily high in the hottest month
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: temp_winter
fields.description: Average nightly low in the coldest month (frost below 0)
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: rain
fields.description: Rain and snow in a year
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: rain_seasonality
fields.description: How unevenly rain falls across the year (Mediterranean: wet winters, dry summers)
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: growing_days
fields.description: Length of the growing season
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: frost_days
fields.description: Days a year the temperature crosses freezing
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: aridity
fields.description: Rain against what the heat could evaporate: under 0.05 desert, 0.2-0.5 semi-arid, over 0.65 humid
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: wind
fields.description: Average wind speed: sailing, winnowing, windbreaks
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: storms
fields.description: Wind speed in the windiest month: storm exposure
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: plant_growth
fields.description: How much plants grow in a year (net primary production)
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: drought_risk
fields.description: Chance in any year of a drought (under two-thirds of the average rain)
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: rain_variability
fields.description: How much the yearly rain varies from year to year
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: clay
fields.description: Clay in the topsoil: holds water and nutrients, heavy to plough
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: sand
fields.description: Sand in the topsoil: drains fast, light to work, poor in nutrients
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: silt
fields.description: Silt in the topsoil: the rich, fine stuff of floodplains and loess
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: organic_matter
fields.description: Organic carbon in the topsoil
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: nitrogen
fields.description: Nitrogen in the topsoil: the main nutrient crops use up
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: ph
fields.description: Acidity: under 5.5 acid, 6-7.5 ideal, over 8 alkaline
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: nutrient_holding
fields.description: How well the soil holds on to nutrients (cation exchange capacity)
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: stones
fields.description: Stones and gravel in the topsoil
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: soil_depth
fields.description: Rooting depth (1 deep, 0 shallow): from stones deep down and slope
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: drainage
fields.description: How fast water drains away (1 fast, 0 waterlogged)
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: fertility
fields.description: Natural fertility: nitrogen, organic matter, nutrient holding, pH
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: salinity
fields.description: Salt in the soil: harms most crops (barley and dates tolerate it)
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)
Facsimilia historical sites (tools/land_sites.json), from standard reference works (project's own)

fields.name: erosion
fields.description: How easily the soil washes away once cleared
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: compaction
fields.description: Dense, compacted soil that roots struggle through
sources: SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (Poggio et al. 2021, SOIL 7:217-240) (CC BY 4.0)

fields.name: river
fields.description: Largest river through the place: 1 great river (Nile, Euphrates), 0.7 major, 0.45 medium, 0.25 small
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: river_km
fields.description: Distance to a medium or larger river
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: lake
fields.description: Share of the place under lakes
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: floodplain
fields.description: Flat land a great river floods: renewed soil, easy irrigation
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: wetland
fields.description: Marsh and delta: reeds, fish, fowl, papyrus - and malaria
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: groundwater
fields.description: How near the water table is: wells, oases, date palms
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: irrigation
fields.description: Water that can be led onto fields
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: springs
fields.description: Springs from wet hills
sources: ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (public domain)

fields.name: water_quality
fields.description: Fresh, clean water (brackish or marsh water is worse)
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: farmed
fields.description: Share of the land farmed or grazed by people in 300 BC
sources: KK10 anthropogenic land cover change (Kaplan et al. 2011, The Holocene 21:775-791) (CC BY 3.0)

fields.name: woodland
fields.description: Share under forest in 300 BC
sources: KK10 anthropogenic land cover change (Kaplan et al. 2011, The Holocene 21:775-791) (CC BY 3.0)

fields.name: conifer
fields.description: How much of the forest is conifer (fir, pine, cedar): ship timber, resin, pitch
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: scrub
fields.description: Share under scrub (maquis, garrigue): browse for goats, herbs, honey
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: grassland
fields.description: Share under grass and steppe: pasture
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)

fields.name: marsh
fields.description: Share under marsh and reeds
sources: Natural Earth 10m rivers and lakes (public domain)

fields.name: desert
fields.description: Share that is bare desert
sources: CHELSA V2.1 climatologies 1981-2010 (Karger et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4:170122) (CC0 1.0)
